A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title. Their complete main text, appendices, equations, algorithms, tables, and figures support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original bilingual TTS evaluations, listening-test results, and emotion, duration, and alignment ablations in Tables 1–7 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original inference-efficiency measurements in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The architecture and controllers are retained. However, v2 Section 5.2 newly specifies three attention heads for MSA, while Equation 1, Appendix B, and Algorithm 1 still select one head as in v1. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents an actual procedural revision or inconsistent documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions use MED-TTS English and Chinese texts, the same seven emotions and three content categories, and ESD speech prompts for emotion and duration control. The added efficiency analysis introduces no new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their comparator sets: MaskGCT, F5-TTS, SparkTTS, CosyVoice2, and IndexTTS2 where applicable, plus the same alignment variants. The efficiency analysis uses the existing baseline and framework components.

E3.justification: v2 adds S1–S3 profiling using real-time factor and autoregressive/end-to-end latency under common RTX 4090 hardware. Appendix A.2 changes stated text-length filters from 15–25 English words and Chinese characters to 25–45 words and 20–30 characters. The unchanged listings retain earlier English limits; dataset regeneration or experimental reruns are not established.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds an incremental component-cost analysis testing the overhead of emotion conditioning and duration steering. Existing emotion/duration ablations, MSA comparisons, and emotion- and category-specific appendix analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain 15-listener MOS means and 95% confidence intervals computed using a t-test in Tables 1–2. No new seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported, including for the added timing results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their values. New Figure 6 and Section 5.2 report full-system RTF increases of 40.2% for English and 42.2% for Chinese over the baseline, while remaining below 1. The new main-text dataset summary reports approximately 12,000 segments per emotion, whereas the retained Appendix A.3 still states 1,200.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 24 corrects the mask indices from segs[t] to segs[r], making the formal update agree with the semantic-token loop and existing Appendix B explanation. The alignment and duration equations and mathematical assumptions are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion newly asserts applicability to a broad class of autoregressive TTS backbones without architectural modification or additional training. The original training-free control and speech-quality claims remain, without new cross-backbone evaluations supporting the broader assertion.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that control overhead mainly arises in autoregressive decoding and preserves real-time operation. Existing explanations of quality tradeoffs and limitations concerning gradual emotion transitions and pretrained duration representations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-repository access information, updates the demo address, and identifies RTX 4090 hardware for profiling. Appendix A.2 removes explicit emotion-description length bounds. LoRA training details and duration-controller hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds introductory citations to Scherer (2003) and Tang et al. (2023). The related-work taxonomy and positioning relative to earlier TTS methods otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 introduces the TED-TTS title and name, expands and retitles Section 3.1 around MED-TTS, adds acknowledgments, and updates contact and corresponding-author information. Most prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the efficiency chart as Figure 6 and moves the dataset-statistics figure from the appendix into Section 3.1. Existing figures are retained with renumbering and relocation; Table 4 also moves, with limited surrounding layout changes.

improvement.justification: The efficiency measurements, code-access information, and corrected masking index improve practical assessment and documentation. However, v2 introduces conflicting three-head versus single-head MSA specifications and changes validation lengths without updating the prompt and review listings. These benefits and reproducibility problems coexist, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
